issues.summary: The "In stock" label is filled with a typed green ("#2E7D32") instead of the success role, so it ignores dark mode.

consequences.note: In dark mode the label's text is the dark on-success colour on the typed green, about 3.3:1 (it needs 4.5:1), so every "In stock" label fails, in both variants and both directions.

issues.summary: The product page's padding (18) isn't on the spacing scale; the other screens use space.s4.
The basket's lines have a typed 10 px corner, which isn't one of the radius roles (the guide gives cards radius.lg).
The product's description sets fontSize: 15 on top of the body role, a size that isn't one of the text roles.
The skeleton's pulse uses a raw Easing.bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) instead of the easing.standard role.
The caption on Sign in saying what the phone number is used for is textSecondary faded to 50%, so it's unreadable: about 2.2:1 in light mode and 2.9:1 in dark (it needs 4.5:1).
Each product's "Add to basket" button is a bare Pressable 32×32 px box instead of IconButton's 44×44, so it's hard to tap.
The shop's sign-in button is an icon in a Pressable with no accessibilityLabel, so a screen reader can't say what it is.

Each product is crammed into its row: 4 px of padding and 4 px gaps, a 40 px picture, names cut to one line, and the pack size gone, so a row no longer says how much you get (a 1 L carton, a tray of 12).

The product page's main action is a hand-made pill (action-secondary fill, body text) instead of AppButton's primary style, so it looks like a supporting action, unlike every other main action, and has no focus ring or pressed state.
The basket has no empty state: with nothing in it, the screen shows an empty list, a total of KWD 0.000 and an active order button, with no way back to the shelves but the back button.

The top bar spaces its title with marginLeft instead of the row's gap (or marginStart), so in Arabic (right to left) the gap is on the wrong side: the title touches the back button, and the space sits on its other side.
The shop's "On the shelves" heading hard-codes Georgia instead of the heading role, so it is a serif unlike every other heading, and in Arabic it loses Readex Pro and falls back to the system's font.
The generated theme code was edited by hand (radius.md changed from 8 to 6), so it no longer matches the design guide, and the next motif tokens will undo it.
